ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Intermittent frontal headaches, episodic shortness of breath, palpitations, bilateral hand tingling; no clear external trigger identified. Symptoms began after starting a new job as a lawyer in London (timeline unspecified but recent).
- Symptom timeline and progression: Headaches occur mainly while at work (during meetings or computer use); palpitations ~ once daily; SOB “sometimes” while seated at desk; symptoms described as new since job change; no clear progression trend provided.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: Denied  
  • Drooling: Not reported  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: Denied  
  • Dyspnea: Episodic shortness of breath while seated; none on exertion  
  • Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): None reported  
  • Ear/neck symptoms: No ear pain, hearing change, or neck swelling reported
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: No previous similar episodes; no prior ED visits, epinephrine, or other acute treatments.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Current medications: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context: Works as a lawyer; reports high work stress (7–8/10). Alcohol ~ 2 glasses wine once weekly. No smoking or recreational drug use. Consultation conducted via telehealth in a private space.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: Not observed (video/telephone consult).
- Airway/breathing descriptors: Patient reports SOB episodes but no audible stridor or respiratory distress noted during call.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert, oriented; denies dizziness/syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (teleconsult).
- Presence of another person: None mentioned.

Assessment:
- Multifactorial symptoms (frontal headaches, palpitations, episodic dyspnea, hand paresthesias) in context of occupational stress and known hyperthyroidism on thyroxine. No current evidence of acute ENT airway compromise or allergic reaction.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person clinic review for full physical examination including cardiopulmonary and focused ENT airway assessment.
- Order blood tests at visit: thyroid function (TSH, free T4), complete blood count, basic metabolic panel.  
- Advise patient to monitor symptom frequency and any escalation (e.g., new throat tightness, voice change, progressive SOB, syncope).  
- Red-flag instructions: If sudden worsening shortness of breath, throat swelling, voice change, or chest pain occurs, call emergency services (dial 999) immediately.  
- Discuss stress management strategies and consider occupational health review at follow-up.  
- No new medications initiated pending examination and labs.  
- Patient will self-book appointment via practice app; clinician to document hand-over for colleague.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing/expected elements: Exact onset date, duration of each episode, thorough ENT review (ear, nasal, throat exam), full allergy list confirmation, auto-injector availability (not indicated but standard for airway complaints), vitals, medication dose/frequency.  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional filler words and minor inaudible gaps but clinical history understandable.
